UNDERSTANDING PRESSURE
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what understanding pressure means in plain words.
• Give one clear example linked to Pressure.
• Correct one common mistake about this page.

INTRODUCTION
----
Understanding Pressure. Get clear on pressure before moving on. How would you explain pressure to a classmate in one minute? Use this anchor: Describe atmospheric pressure as used in Physics,. Clue from the topic: Factors affecting pressure in. Check every example on this page against that anchor.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Pressure is force acting normally per unit area.
• P = F / A, with P in pascals (Pa = N/m²).
• For the same force, a smaller area gives a larger pressure (why a sharp knife cuts easily).
• Atmospheric pressure and liquid pressure also matter in physics — liquid pressure increases with depth.
• Always use SI units: force in newtons, area in square metres, before substituting.

WORKED EXAMPLE
----
Worked example — pressure:
A force of 260 N acts normally on an area of 0.25 m². Find the pressure.

Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 260 / 0.25
3. P = 1040
Final Answer: 1040 Pa
